'Defense Reaction - Destroy Amulet of Havencall: Search your deck for a card named Rally the Rearguard, add it to this chain link as a defending card, then shuffle. Activate this ability only if you have no cards in hand.'

Verified end to end. DEFENSE_REACTION activations on items are offered by play._add_dsl_activations to the DEFENDER in the reaction step (play.py ~290-302), which also evaluates ability 'conditions' at offer time (~307) - so the 'only if you have no cards in hand' restriction gates legality, not just resolution. HAND_SIZE_EQ is a real condition (condition_types.py ~1091) reading 'amount'; amount 0 means an exactly-empty hand. The triage note's primitive name was right.

'Destroy Amulet of Havencall' is the ability-level cost [{DESTROY_SELF}] (cost_types.py ~43), paid by _apply_activate_card before run_ability (play.py ~1291-1296); reaction abilities then run directly (~1303-1312).

The search: SEARCH_DECK (effect_types.py ~1616) reads 'name' and shuffles before placement; it has NO 'add to this chain link as a defending card' destination, so the clause is expressed as search-into-hand followed by ADD_DEFEND with an object target resolving a card NAMED Rally the Rearguard from HAND (_compile_object_target reads controller/zone/name/amount; effect_types.py ~623). add_defend (effect_keywords.py ~4010) removes the card from its current zone - typically hand - onto combat.defending_cards and credits its {d}, so the END state matches the printed text; the intermediate hand stop happens inside one ability resolution. If the deck has no Rally the Rearguard, ask_optional's fail-to-find leaves the hand unchanged and ADD_DEFEND's pool comes back empty, so nothing is added.

Printed **Go again** fires from the card DB keywords field - deliberately NOT re-authored here. Note for reviewers: Rally the Rearguard needs its own JSON definition (and the engine must allow playing a defending card already on the chain) for the fetched card to actually block with its effect; that is that card's implementation, not this one.
